memory_candidates.content: When narrowing an automated `git add "$task_dir/"`-style whole-directory staging call to exclude a few ephemeral file classes, prefer git exclusion pathspecs (`:(exclude)path`) appended to the same `git add` invocation over rewriting it as an allowlist. Live task directories accumulate directories an allowlist author won't anticipate (progress/, handoffs/, fixtures/, tests/, loose top-level .md files) — an allowlist silently stops staging all of them, trading one silent-drop bug for another. Exclusion pathspecs subtract exactly the named ephemeral paths and nothing else, and compose cleanly across multiple staging call sites that share one canonical exclusion array.

The decisive test for whether a runtime scratch file should be gitignored (vs. tracked as durable provenance) is not 'is it overwritten each cycle' but 'does its reader apply a freshness gate (session_id or mtime-vs-dispatch-window check) before trusting it'. A file with no freshness gate is unsafe to ever restore from git history — a stale git-restored copy would be silently trusted — so it must be gitignored regardless of how disciplined its own writer/cleanup logic is. A file with a documented freshness gate (mtime vs. dispatch_start_ts, or an equivalent window check) safely tolerates being git-tracked, because a restored stale copy simply fails the gate and is treated as absent.

When multiple orchestrate/implement agents run concurrently against the same git working tree, `git add <specific paths>` can land on top of another session's already-staged (but not yet committed) changes, since the git index is a single shared file. Before committing, always run `git diff --staged --name-only` to check for unexpected extra paths. If contamination is found, `git reset` (mixed, not --hard) safely unstages everything without touching the working tree, after which the intended paths can be re-added and committed precisely — the other session's staged-but-uncommitted work remains present in the working tree and can be re-staged by that session later.
